name: InteractiveHoverButton
description: A button whose label slides away to an arrow, or to a second label with an arrow, on hover and keyboard focus. Builds on Button.

children.description: Button label. This is the accessible name.

hoverLabel.description: Optional wording shown on hover and focus, next to the arrow. It is visual only and should say the same thing as the label. Without it only the arrow appears.

size.description: Height, padding and font size, as on Button.

isDisabled.description: Prevents interaction, dims the button and turns the effect off.

isLoading.description: Shows a spinner and blocks presses; the pending state is announced.

onPress.description: Called when the button is pressed by mouse, touch or keyboard.

keyboard: Tab focuses it and shows the same effect as hover
requirements: The effect is the same for mouse hover and keyboard focus (focus-visible), so keyboard users see it too
The alternate label and arrow are decoration, hidden from assistive technology; the accessible name is always the main label
On touch screens there is no hover, so the button stays still
Stands still for visitors who ask for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion), and inside an rdm-still container
A disabled or loading button does not animate
The arrow flips in right-to-left layouts
Optional: it is a separate component, so projects that do not add it carry none of its code
screenReader: Announced exactly as a Button: its label, as a button; the effect adds nothing to what is read

use_when: A call to action on a landing page that should feel responsive
A link-like action that leads somewhere, where the arrow adds meaning
avoid_when: Dense toolbars or forms, where plain Button is calmer
Destructive actions, where a changing label could confuse
anti_patterns: A hover label that says something different from the main label
A hover label much longer than the main label: it is clipped to the button's width
